title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 62 (Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract)

content.overview: Section 62 provides that if the parties to a contract agree to substitute a new contract for it, or to rescind or alter it, the original contract need not be performed.
content.glance: Novation, rescission or alteration by agreement → original contract need not be performed.
content.study: If the parties agree to substitute a new contract (novation), rescind the contract, or alter it, the original contract need not be performed. Novation may change obligations or substitute a party with consent. Current-law framing: identify agreement to substitute, rescind or alter; conclude original need not be performed.

sections.heading: Novation
sections.body: Agreement to substitute a new contract for the original — original need not be performed.

sections.heading: Rescission
sections.body: Agreement to rescind — original need not be performed.

sections.heading: Alteration
sections.body: Agreement to alter — original need not be performed to the extent altered.

provisions.title: Effect of novation, rescission, and alteration of contract

examples.title: Novation of debtor
examples.body: A owes B under a contract. A, B and C agree that B will accept C as debtor instead of A. The old debt ends; a new debt from C to B arises under s. 62.

hypotheticals.question: Does a unilateral change by one party amount to novation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 62 requires agreement of the parties to substitute, rescind or alter.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-62
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Any change in terms automatically discharges the original contract without agreement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 62 requires the parties to agree to substitute, rescind or alter.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 62 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify agreement to substitute, rescind or alter. II. Conclude original need not be performed. III. Identify the new obligations if any. IV. Conclude.
